# The service levels in Kestrel's contract with Brannock City Transport.
# The shape follows the service levels in Citi Bike's monthly report to New York City:
# https://mot-marketing-whitelabel-prod.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/nyc/April-2026-Citi-Bike-Monthly-Report.pdf
# Nobody edits this file except the city. Claude Code must never change it.
contract: Brannock City Transport and Kestrel Bike Share
service_levels:
  - id: SLA-4
    name: Bike defects
    rule: A rider pressing the wrench button is notice of a defect.
    clock_starts: when the rider reports the defect (the wrench)
    wrenched_limit_hours: 48
    not_wrenched_limit_hours: 96
    target_percent: 95
    credit_per_late_bike_gbp: 50
  - id: SLA-9
    name: Bike availability
    rule: The share of the fleet that riders can rent, across every district.
    minimum_percent: 96
  - id: SLA-11
    name: Station outage
    rule: No single station outage lasts longer than this.
    limit_hours: 4
  - id: SLA-12
    name: Public feed accuracy
    rule: Real-time data in the public feed is accurate and available to the public at all times.
    feed_max_age_seconds: 60
---

name: city-contract
description: Kestrel's contract with Brannock City Transport. Use it whenever you write a spec, a plan or code that touches wrench reports, the public feed or the crew queue.
---

# The city contract

The contract is in `data/contract/sla.yaml`. Read it. Never edit it.

- **The 48 hour clock starts at the wrench.** A wrenched bike must be fixed within 48 hours of the report, not 48 hours after the job is opened.
- **Defects a crew finds itself get 96 hours.** The clock starts when the crew reports it.
- **The public feed is accurate at all times.** A broken bike must show `is_disabled: true` within 60 seconds. A grace period breaks this rule.
- **Late bikes cost money.** Each late wrenched bike costs a credit of 50 pounds.

If a request conflicts with the contract, do not build it. Write the conflict down and ask the product manager.
# Plan: build the approved spec

Made in plan mode from `work/spec.md`. Claude Code read the code, then wrote this plan. No file changed until it was approved.

## Files that change

- `src/wrenches.ts`
- `src/crew-queue.ts`
- `src/database.ts`

## Order of work

- **P-1** Disable the bike when a wrench arrives, in `src/wrenches.ts`. Serves AC-1 and AC-2.
- **P-2** Start the deadline clock at the wrench `reported_at`, in `src/crew-queue.ts`. Serves AC-4.
- **P-3** Sort the queue by deadline, due first, in `src/crew-queue.ts`. Serves AC-3.

## Risks

- P-1 is the riskiest step: if the update fails, the bike stays rentable. The acceptance test for AC-1 catches it.
- Sorting must not drop jobs. AC-3 checks the order on all open jobs.

## Proof

- `bun test` passes, including `test/acceptance/`.
- `bun run world`, then `bun run world wrench B-2207` shows `is_disabled: true`.
# Findings: why wrenched bikes miss the 48 hour limit

Claude Code read `data/wrenches.csv` and `data/repairs.csv`: 90 days, 2,160 wrench reports.

| Number                                                                | Value                                      | How it was found                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Wrenched bikes fixed late (over 48 hours)                             | 118 of 2,160, which is 5.46%               | `bun -e` script: count jobs where `closed_at` minus `reported_at` is over 48 hours          |
| Contract target met                                                   | 94.54%, under the 95% target               | the same script, 100 minus the miss rate                                                    |
| Late bikes that are e-bikes with a BATT fault at North depot stations | 67 of 118, which is 56.8%                  | join `wrenches.csv` to `stations.csv` on `station_id`, filter `bike_type`, `fault`, `depot` |
| Wrenched bikes rented again before a crew reached them                | 193 of 2,160, which is 8.94%               | count rows with a value in `rented_again_at`                                                |
| Contract credits for late bikes                                       | 118 times 50 pounds, which is 5,900 pounds | late count times `credit_per_late_bike_gbp` in `data/contract/sla.yaml`                     |

## What this means

The misses are not spread out. More than half are battery faults on e-bikes near the North depot.
A battery fault does not look broken, so the next rider takes the bike. The feed still shows it as rentable.
The North crews work the oldest job first, not the job that is due first.

More crews would cost money every month. Taking the bike out of the feed and sorting the queue by deadline costs one change.

input.content:
# Reviewing changes to spoke

How to review a change to Kestrel spoke, by a person or by a coding agent.
The rules in `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` still apply. This file says what a reviewer checks.

Block the change if any **Blocker** below fails. Other problems are comments, and the author decides.

## 1. Protected files — Blocker

- [ ] No change under `data/contract/`. The city owns the contract. If the code needs a different rule, the code is wrong or the PM must go to the city.
- [ ] No change under `test/acceptance/` after QA approved it (see `work/approvals.jsonl`). A failing acceptance test means change the code.
- [ ] No new or edited line in `work/approvals.jsonl` written by an agent. Only a person approves, through `bun run approve`.
- [ ] No change to an approved `work/` file (intent, spec, decision, plan) unless the change comes with a new approval. Check that its sha256 still matches `work/approvals.jsonl`:
  ```sh
  sha256sum work/plan.md   # compare with the "sha256" for work/plan.md
  ```
- [ ] No change to `.claude/settings.json` that loosens the `deny` or `ask` rules.

## 2. Traceability to the approved plan — Blocker

- [ ] Each commit serves one plan item, and its message starts with the item id, for example `P-2: ...`.
- [ ] The change only touches files `work/plan.md` lists under "Files that change". Any other file needs a reason in the PR, or a plan update with a new approval.
- [ ] The change does what the plan item and its acceptance criteria in `work/spec.md` say, and nothing more. Extra features wait for their own spec.
- [ ] Each commit is under 200 changed lines (`git show --stat <sha>`).

## 3. The city contract — Blocker

Read `data/contract/sla.yaml` before reviewing code in `src/wrenches.ts`, `src/feed.ts` or `src/crew-queue.ts`.

- [ ] **SLA-4: the clock starts at the wrench.** Deadlines are computed from `reported_at`, never from `opened_at`. A wrench gets 48 hours; a defect a crew finds gets 96 hours. This is the mistake agents make most often in this repo.
- [ ] **SLA-12: the feed is accurate at all times.** A wrenched bike shows `is_disabled: true` straight away. No grace period, no cache, no batch job that delays it past 60 seconds.
- [ ] **The wrench is atomic.** The wrench row, the repair job and `is_disabled = 1` are written in one transaction. A failure must never leave a broken bike rentable.
- [ ] **The crew queue never drops jobs.** Sorting and filtering keep every open job for the depot. The job due first goes on top.
- [ ] Contract numbers (48, 96, 60, 50) match `sla.yaml`. Prefer reading them from the contract over a new hard-coded copy.

If a change conflicts with the contract, do not approve it with a workaround. Ask for the conflict to be written down and sent to the PM.

## 4. Public feed — Blocker for field names

- [ ] Feed field names follow GBFS v3: snake_case, for example `is_disabled`, `num_vehicles_available`, `num_vehicles_disabled`. No invented names, no renamed fields.
- [ ] Removing or changing the meaning of a feed field is a breaking change for outside apps. It needs a decision record in `work/decisions/`.
- [ ] Station counts agree with the bikes table: a disabled bike counts as disabled, not available.

## 5. Correctness and code

- [ ] SQL uses bound parameters (`?`, `?1`). No values joined into a query string.
- [ ] Times are stored and compared as UTC ISO 8601 strings (`toISOString()`). Watch for local time and for sorting dates as text in mixed formats.
- [ ] Requests with a missing or unknown `bike_id`, `station_id` or `depot` return a clear 4xx, not a crash.
- [ ] Every new route is listed in `src/server.ts`.
- [ ] Changes to seeding in `src/database.ts` still work on a fresh start and on an existing database.
- [ ] Comments say why, and name the SLA when a rule comes from the contract (as in `src/crew-queue.ts`).
- [ ] Events that matter to operations (wrench, repair, disable) are logged with `logEvent`.

## 6. Tests

- [ ] `bun test` passes, including `test/acceptance/`. Run it yourself; do not trust the PR text.
- [ ] New behaviour has a unit test in `test/`, outside `test/acceptance/`.
- [ ] Tests that touch the contract check the edge: a job at exactly 48 hours, a crew-found defect, a tie on deadline.
- [ ] No test skipped, weakened, or made to pass by changing what it checks.

## 7. Release

- [ ] Nobody ran `bun run deploy:production` before the release manager approved `work/rollout.yaml`.
- [ ] The PR says how to check the change after release and that `bun run rollback` is the way back.

## How to write review comments

- Say what is wrong, where (`src/file.ts:line`), and why. Name the SLA, acceptance criterion or plan item it breaks.
- Mark each comment **Blocker** or **Suggestion**.
- Point to the approved file that settles the question rather than arguing taste. If no approved file settles it, it is a suggestion.

# Reviewing changes to spoke

How to review a change to Kestrel spoke, by a person or by a coding agent.
The rules in `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` still apply. This file says what a reviewer checks.

Block the change if any **Blocker** below fails. Other problems are comments, and the author decides.

## 1. Protected files — Blocker

- [ ] No change under `data/contract/`. The city owns the contract. If the code needs a different rule, the code is wrong or the PM must go to the city.
- [ ] No change under `test/acceptance/` after QA approved it (see `work/approvals.jsonl`). A failing acceptance test means change the code.
- [ ] No new or edited line in `work/approvals.jsonl` written by an agent. Only a person approves, through `bun run approve`.
- [ ] No change to an approved `work/` file (intent, spec, decision, plan) unless the change comes with a new approval. Check that its sha256 still matches `work/approvals.jsonl`:
  ```sh
  sha256sum work/plan.md   # compare with the "sha256" for work/plan.md
  ```
- [ ] No change to `.claude/settings.json` that loosens the `deny` or `ask` rules.

## 2. Traceability to the approved plan — Blocker

- [ ] Each commit serves one plan item, and its message starts with the item id, for example `P-2: ...`.
- [ ] The change only touches files `work/plan.md` lists under "Files that change". Any other file needs a reason in the PR, or a plan update with a new approval.
- [ ] The change does what the plan item and its acceptance criteria in `work/spec.md` say, and nothing more. Extra features wait for their own spec.
- [ ] Each commit is under 200 changed lines (`git show --stat <sha>`).

## 3. The city contract — Blocker

Read `data/contract/sla.yaml` before reviewing code in `src/wrenches.ts`, `src/feed.ts` or `src/crew-queue.ts`.

- [ ] **SLA-4: the clock starts at the wrench.** Deadlines are computed from `reported_at`, never from `opened_at`. A wrench gets 48 hours; a defect a crew finds gets 96 hours. This is the mistake agents make most often in this repo.
- [ ] **SLA-12: the feed is accurate at all times.** A wrenched bike shows `is_disabled: true` straight away. No grace period, no cache, no batch job that delays it past 60 seconds.
- [ ] **The wrench is atomic.** The wrench row, the repair job and `is_disabled = 1` are written in one transaction. A failure must never leave a broken bike rentable.
- [ ] **The crew queue never drops jobs.** Sorting and filtering keep every open job for the depot. The job due first goes on top.
- [ ] Contract numbers (48, 96, 60, 50) match `sla.yaml`. Prefer reading them from the contract over a new hard-coded copy.

If a change conflicts with the contract, do not approve it with a workaround. Ask for the conflict to be written down and sent to the PM.

## 4. Public feed — Blocker for field names

- [ ] Feed field names follow GBFS v3: snake_case, for example `is_disabled`, `num_vehicles_available`, `num_vehicles_disabled`. No invented names, no renamed fields.
- [ ] Removing or changing the meaning of a feed field is a breaking change for outside apps. It needs a decision record in `work/decisions/`.
- [ ] Station counts agree with the bikes table: a disabled bike counts as disabled, not available.

## 5. Correctness and code

- [ ] SQL uses bound parameters (`?`, `?1`). No values joined into a query string.
- [ ] Times are stored and compared as UTC ISO 8601 strings (`toISOString()`). Watch for local time and for sorting dates as text in mixed formats.
- [ ] Requests with a missing or unknown `bike_id`, `station_id` or `depot` return a clear 4xx, not a crash.
- [ ] Every new route is listed in `src/server.ts`.
- [ ] Changes to seeding in `src/database.ts` still work on a fresh start and on an existing database.
- [ ] Comments say why, and name the SLA when a rule comes from the contract (as in `src/crew-queue.ts`).
- [ ] Events that matter to operations (wrench, repair, disable) are logged with `logEvent`.

## 6. Tests

- [ ] `bun test` passes, including `test/acceptance/`. Run it yourself; do not trust the PR text.
- [ ] New behaviour has a unit test in `test/`, outside `test/acceptance/`.
- [ ] Tests that touch the contract check the edge: a job at exactly 48 hours, a crew-found defect, a tie on deadline.
- [ ] No test skipped, weakened, or made to pass by changing what it checks.

## 7. Release

- [ ] Nobody ran `bun run deploy:production` before the release manager approved `work/rollout.yaml`.
- [ ] The PR says how to check the change after release and that `bun run rollback` is the way back.

## How to write review comments

- Say what is wrong, where (`src/file.ts:line`), and why. Name the SLA, acceptance criterion or plan item it breaks.
- Mark each comment **Blocker** or **Suggestion**.
- Point to the approved file that settles the question rather than arguing taste. If no approved file settles it, it is a suggestion.

2. **Matches the approved plan:** commit messages start with the plan item id (`P-n:`). Changes stay within the files and scope that `work/plan.md` lists, and each commit is under 200 changed lines.
3. **City contract:**
   - Deadlines count from `reported_at`, never from `opened_at`. This is called out as the most common agent mistake.
   - The feed shows a wrenched bike as disabled within 60 seconds, with no grace period.
   - The wrench row, the repair job and the disable are written in one transaction.
   - The crew queue never drops jobs.
   - The numbers in the code match `sla.yaml`.
4. **Public feed:** field names follow GBFS v3. Removing a field or changing its meaning needs a decision record.
5. **Code checks:** SQL uses bound parameters, times are UTC ISO strings, bad input gets a 4xx, new routes are listed in `src/server.ts`, and seeding still works on a fresh start and an existing database.

7. **Release:** no deploy before `work/rollout.yaml` is approved, and the PR names `bun run rollback` as the way back.

It ends with a short guide on writing review comments.
